+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Algebra.Decoding
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Witnesses
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Extraction.Defs
+
+/-!
+# Pulled-apart Pauli observables
+
+This module constructs the measurements and observables used to pull the two
+Pauli bases onto separate registers. The construction retains the distinct
+local spaces of the two players and uses the binary basis fixed in the
+canonical field model.
+
+## References
+
+The product form and observable relations formalize `lem:tildew-product-form`
+in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:75-88`, from
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1415-1456`.
+The swap identities formalize
+`lem:v-swap-conjugation`, blueprint lines 208-243 and paper lines 1687-1713.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-! ## Pulled-apart measurements and observables -/
+
+namespace PauliKind
+
+/-- Select the polynomial belonging to a Pauli basis from a joint polynomial
+outcome. This is the marginalization used at paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1421-1423` and blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:35-44`. -/
+def selectPoly {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind) : PolyPair P -> Poly P
+  | pair => match W with
+    | .X => pair.1
+    | .Z => pair.2
+
+end PauliKind
+
+namespace GlobalPairWitness
+
+/-- The single-basis marginal of the global polynomial-pair measurement.
+This is `def:s-w-marginals`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:35-44`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1421-1423`. -/
+noncomputable def marginalPoly {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) :
+    Measurement (Poly P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
+  (w.Smeas side).postprocess W.selectPoly
+
+/-- The single-basis marginal remains a projective measurement. This is the
+projectivity assertion implicit in `def:s-w-marginals`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:35-44`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1421-1423`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the preservation of projectivity under
+the finite postprocessing map `PauliKind.selectPoly`. -/
+theorem marginalPoly_isProjective {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) :
+    Measurement.IsProjective (w.marginalPoly side W) := by
+  sorry
+
+end GlobalPairWitness
+
+/-- The pulled-apart projective-measurement effect from Equation `eq:tilde_M`.
+The polynomial marginal acts on the player's expanded local space and the
+dot-product projector acts on the newly adjoined register. Blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:55-62`; paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1425-1435`. -/
+noncomputable def tildeM {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P)
+    (a : PauliScalar P) : Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side)) :=
+  ∑ g : Poly P,
+    heteroKron ((w.marginalPoly side W).effect g)
+      (tauDotProj W u (dotProduct (decodeFq g) u - a))
+
+/-- Each pulled-apart effect is a projector, as asserted in
+`def:tilde-m-measurement`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:55-62`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1425-1435`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the orthogonal-sum calculation using
+`marginalPoly_isProjective` and `tauDotProj_isProj`. -/
+theorem tildeM_isProj {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P)
+    (a : PauliScalar P) :
+    IsProj (tildeM w side W u a) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- The pulled-apart effects are complete for each fixed basis and Pauli
+register vector. This is the completeness assertion in
+`def:tilde-m-measurement`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:55-62`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1425-1435`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks summing the orthogonal dot-product
+projectors and the polynomial marginal effects. -/
+theorem sum_tildeM_eq_one {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P) :
+    ∑ a : PauliScalar P, tildeM w side W u a = 1 := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- The binary observable obtained from the trace coarse-graining of `tildeM`.
+This is Equation `eq:def-tildewj` in `def:tilde-w-observables`, blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:64-71`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1437-1442`. -/
+noncomputable def tildeObs {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P)
+    (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) : Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side)) :=
+  ∑ a : PauliScalar P,
+    phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (P.model.basis j * a)) •
+      tildeM w side W u a
+
+/-- Product form of the pulled-apart observable, Equation
+`eq:tildewj-product-form` of `lem:tildew-product-form`. Blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:75-88`; paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1442-1450`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the finite Fourier regrouping needed to
+derive this equality from `tauObservable_eq_sum_pauliProj`. Discharge: expand
+the two finite sums and reindex the Pauli outcomes by their dot product. -/
+theorem tildeObs_eq_heteroKron {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P)
+    (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) :
+    tildeObs w side W u j =
+      heteroKron
+        (∑ pair : PolyPair P,
+          phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model
+            (P.model.basis j * dotProduct (decodeFq (W.selectPoly pair)) u)) •
+            (w.Smeas side).effect pair)
+        (tauObservable W (P.model.basis j • u)) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Every pulled-apart observable is Hermitian, as asserted in
+`lem:tildew-product-form`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:75-88`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1450`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks this consequence of the product form.
+Discharge: use projectivity of `w.Smeas side` and Hermiticity of the generalized
+Pauli observable. -/
+theorem tildeObs_isHermitian {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P)
+    (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) :
+    (tildeObs w side W u j).IsHermitian := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- Every pulled-apart observable squares to the identity, as asserted in
+`lem:tildew-product-form`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:75-88`, paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1450`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks this consequence of the product form.
+Discharge: eliminate cross terms using the orthogonality of `w.Smeas side` and
+use that `tauObservable` is self-inverse. -/
+theorem tildeObs_mul_self {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon delta : ℝ}
+    {S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon} (w : GlobalPairWitness S delta)
+    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P)
+    (j : Fin P.model.basisDim) :
+    tildeObs w side W u j * tildeObs w side W u j = 1 := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- The corrected twisted commutation relation for pulled-apart observables.

+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Extraction.Consistency
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.SoundnessDefs
+
+/-!
+# Extraction by the swap unitaries
+
+The concrete swap operators below yield the Pauli extraction conclusion. The
+local maps are constructed from the global polynomial
+measurements, and all operators retain the heterogeneous Alice and Bob
+placements. The generalized Pauli projectors use the field and basis fixed by
+`P.model`.
+
+## References
+
+The extraction witness formalizes `lem:qld-unitary` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:295-314`, from
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1860`.
+The error-form comparison formalizes `lem:qld-extraction-error-form` and
+supports `rem:pauli-robustness-form` in the blueprint; its paper source is
+lines 1855-1858 and 1868-1876.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-- The concrete conclusion of `lem:qld-unitary`: the two swap maps extract an
+EPR state and conjugate each player's total Pauli measurement to the canonical
+Pauli projectors. The answer sum in `pauli_close` is over
+`PauliRegister P`; the uniform distribution on `Unit` records that there is no
+average over questions.
+
+Blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:295-314`; paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685,1827-1859`. The swap maps
+are `swapUnitary w .alice` and `swapUnitary w .bob`, defined from the
+side-indexed global measurements, and use only the basis fixed by `P.model`.
+-/
+structure ExtractionWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaS : ℝ}
+    (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon) (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaS)
+    (delta : ℝ) where
+  /-- Each swap map is a right unitary. -/
+  swap_right_unitary : ∀ side : PlayerSide,
+    swapUnitary w side * (swapUnitary w side)ᴴ = 1
+  /-- Each swap map is a left unitary. -/
+  swap_left_unitary : ∀ side : PlayerSide,
+    (swapUnitary w side)ᴴ * swapUnitary w side = 1
+  /-- The auxiliary state on registers `AA'BB'`. -/
+  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ
+    (ExtractionAuxRegisters P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
+  /-- The auxiliary state is normalized. -/
+  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
+  /-- Applying both concrete swap maps to the expanded state extracts the ideal
+  auxiliary-state/EPR tensor product. -/
+  state_close :
+    ‖S.applyBoth (swapUnitary w .alice) (swapUnitary w .bob) S.psiHat -
+        S.idealExpState aux‖ ^ 2 ≤ delta
+  /-- On the ideal extracted state, conjugated total-Pauli effects are close to
+  the canonical projectors, for both players and both Pauli bases. -/
+  pauli_close : ∀ (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind),
+    opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
+      (fun (_ : Unit) (h : PauliRegister P) =>
+        conjBy (S.placeSide side (swapUnitary w side))
+          (S.placePlayer side ((S.pauliMeas side W).effect h)))
+      (fun (_ : Unit) (h : PauliRegister P) =>
+        S.placeExtractedRegister side (pauliProj W h))
+      (S.idealExpState aux) ≤ delta
+
+/-- `lem:qld-unitary`: the concrete swap maps admit extraction data at the
+explicit extraction scale applied to `deltaConstructPaulis`.
+
+This is the source-facing existence statement from blueprint
+`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:295-314` and paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1860`. It introduces no transfer
+premise or additional basis parameter.
+
+**Local fix:** the positive-contraction estimate and normalization case split
+repair the two numerical defects at paper lines 1743-1783 without changing the
+conclusion; see `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_extraction-transfer.tex`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks the EPR projection argument and the
+Schwartz-Zippel comparison at paper lines 1715-1858. Discharge: construct
+`aux` from the EPR projection of the swapped state, use the corrected
+small-error case split, and combine the point-measurement consistency with the
+exact swap conjugation identities. -/
+theorem exists_extractionWitness :
+    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
+      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon deltaG : ℝ),
+        0 ≤ epsilon → epsilon ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ deltaG →
+          ∀ (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon)
+            (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG),
+            Nonempty
+              (ExtractionWitness S w
+                (deltaExtract C
+                  (deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon deltaG P.m P.d P.q)
+                  P.m P.d P.q)) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- The composed construction and extraction errors preserve the error family
+of `thm:pauli`: when `deltaG` has the form
+`deltaQld a b epsilon m d q`, the result is bounded by another member of that
+family after decreasing the exponent and enlarging the universal constant.
+
+This is `lem:qld-extraction-error-form` in the blueprint and the named
+quantitative obligation behind `rem:pauli-robustness-form`; the concluding
+paper comparison is at
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1855-1858,1868-1876`.
+
+**Proof obligation:** issue #47 tracks this real-power estimate. Discharge:
+take an exponent no larger than `b / 4` and `1 / 8`, bound the fourth root of
+the terms in `deltaConstructPaulis`, absorb `md/q` using admissibility, and
+enlarge the prefactor and polynomial exponent. -/
+theorem deltaExtract_le_deltaQld (C a b : ℝ) (hC : 1 ≤ C) (ha : 1 < a)
+    (hb : 0 < b) (hb1 : b < 1) :
+    ∃ a' b' : ℝ, 1 ≤ a' ∧ 0 < b' ∧ b' < 1 ∧
+      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon : ℝ), 0 ≤ epsilon →
+        epsilon ≤ 1 →
+        deltaExtract C
+            (deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon
+              (deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q) P.m P.d P.q)
+            P.m P.d P.q ≤
+          deltaQld a' b' epsilon P.m P.d P.q := by
+  sorry
+
+end
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    53	converse is asserted.

    74	and $s$, with all remaining coordinates zero, gives
    75	$\widetilde u\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde v=s$.  The two extracted observables
    76	then anticommute.  This is a counterexample to the printed cross-basis
    77	commutation assertion.

    79	When $\widetilde u\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde v$ lies in the prime field, the
    80	printed distinction is recovered from self-duality.  The chapter quantifies
    81	over arbitrary vectors, however, so that special case does not repair its
    82	statement.

    20	
    21	\begin{itemize}
    22	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The source quotes a fiberwise consequence

    24	  and a compatibility argument for the auxiliary spaces.

    30	  quantum linearity theorem and its state-dependent metric are project-level

    38	\section{Key theorem forms}
    39	
    40	Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let $\rho$ be an arbitrary
    41	density operator on $H$, and let $u\mapsto O^u$ be binary observables on $H$,
    42	indexed by $\mathbb F_2^t$.  The cited theorem assumes the averaged
    43	correlation estimate
    44	\[
    45	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u,v}
    46	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left(O^u O^v O^{u+v}\rho\right) \geq 1-\delta.
    47	\]
    48	It produces an auxiliary space $H'$, a unit vector $\mathrm{anc}\in H'$, and
    49	binary observables $L^u$ on $H\otimes H'$ satisfying, with
    50	$\rho'=\rho\otimes|\mathrm{anc}\rangle\langle\mathrm{anc}|$,
    51	\[
    52	  L^uL^v=L^{u+v}
    53	  \quad\text{for every }u,v.
    54	\]
    55	Moreover,
    56	\[
    57	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u}
    58	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left((L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})^\dagger
    59	    (L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})\,\rho'\right)\leq\delta.
    60	\]
    61	In particular, $L^0=I$: exact linearity gives $(L^0)^2=L^0$, while an
    62	observable is invertible.
    63	
    64	The chapter needs a parameterized version.  For each pair $(x,z)$ it applies
    65	the theorem to $(r,s)\mapsto O^{x,z,r,s}$.  Since the provider theorem accepts
    66	the actual nonnegative defect on each fiber, no assumption that a fiber defect
    67	is at most one, and no good--bad fiber split, is needed.  One must still
    68	formulate the finite common-extension step that makes the auxiliary space
    69	uniform over $(x,z)$.
    70	
    71	\section{Comparison with the quoted statement}
    72	
    73	Lines~711--725 of
    74	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex} quote the
    75	linearity theorem.  The displayed hypothesis correctly averages over both
    76	group variables.  The displayed conclusion, however, says that the corrected
    77	observable is close for every $u$, whereas Theorem~10 of the cited work gives
    78	closeness only on average over $u$ \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}.  The quotation
    79	also inserts $\delta\leq1$, which is absent from the provider theorem and would
    80	unnecessarily obstruct applying it with a fiber's actual defect.  The assertion
    81	at the identity follows from exact linearity as above.
    82	
    83	Lines~825--832 construct the family $O^{x,z,r,s}$ and establish approximate
    84	linearity only after averaging over $x,z,r,r',s,s'$.  They then apply the
    85	single-family theorem separately for every $(x,z)$ and state that sufficiently
    86	many zero ancillas avoid a further extension.  The remaining implicit step is
    87	to make the theorem's possibly fiber-dependent auxiliary spaces uniform.
    88	
    89	The finite setting admits a standard repair.  Apply the theorem on each fiber
    90	with its actual defect, choose one finite auxiliary space large enough for all
    91	returned spaces, and embed each returned space so that its unit vector maps to
    92	one fixed vector.  Extend the conjugated observables by the identity on the
    93	orthogonal complement.  The embeddings may depend on the fiber because the
    94	observables do.  Averaging then yields the conclusion used later in the
    95	chapter.  This is an open reduction, not a counterexample to the quoted theorem
    96	or to the source's eventual combined-measurement conclusion.

    98	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
    99	
   100	Theorem~\path{thm:linearity} and
   101	Remark~\path{rem:linearity-import} in
   102	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex} record respectively the
   103	averaged provider theorem and the common-ancilla obligation for its fiberwise

   106	The declaration \path{exists_exactly_linear_observables} in
   107	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean} assumes a nonnegative defect, a
   108	positive semidefinite trace-one operator, binary observables, and the averaged

   110	normalized ancillary vector for that family, exactly linear binary observables
   111	on the extension, and only the averaged squared-distance bound with the same
   112	defect.  It neither assumes $\delta\leq1$ nor asserts pointwise closeness.  Its
   113	statement therefore matches the provider-faithful blueprint theorem rather
   114	than the strengthened quotation in the QPBT paper.  Its proof remains open,

   123	\section{Conclusion}
   124	
   125	The primary discrepancy is a quantifier mismatch in the quotation: the cited
   126	linearity theorem gives average, not pointwise, closeness.  Its use for the
   127	family indexed by $(x,z)$ also requires an explicit finite common-extension
   128	argument.  Both are open formal reductions compatible with the intended

    18	
    19	\section{At a glance}
    20	
    21	\begin{itemize}
    22	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The extraction proof contains two
    23	  incorrect numerical steps and later suppresses the range projection when
    24	  passing from unitary conjugation to isometry conjugation.
    25	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} A corrected positive-contraction estimate,
    26	  a small-error case split for normalization, and one range-projection transfer
    27	  lemma for a projective measurement family.
    28	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Positivity, contraction inequalities,
    29	  isometry range projections, and norm estimates belong to finite-dimensional
    30	  Hilbert-space algebra.  The state-dependent family distance and register
    31	  placements are project-local.
    32	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} The inequality
    33	  $H^2\geq2H-I$ for a positive contraction, the triangle inequality, and
    34	  $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$ for an isometry.  The repair is tracked in
    35	  \ghissue{19}.
    36	\end{itemize}
    37	
    38	\section{Key theorem forms}
    39	
    40	Let $H_X$ and $H_Z$ be the positive contractions of the extraction proof, and
    41	let $\vartheta$ be a unit vector such that
    42	\[
    43	  \langle\vartheta,H_W\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta/2
    44	  \qquad (W\in\{X,Z\}).
    45	\]
    46	Since $(I-H_W)^2\geq0$,
    47	\[
    48	  H_W^2\geq2H_W-I,
    49	  \qquad
    50	  \langle\vartheta,H_W^2\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta.
    51	\]
    52	Also $\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert^2\leq\delta$, whence
    53	\[
    54	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert^2\leq4\delta.
    55	\]
    56	Together with $H_XH_Z$ equal to the EPR projection, these estimates give the
    57	required overlap bound, with constants absorbed into the stated
    58	$O(\sqrt\delta)$ error.
    59	
    60	For the final transfer, let $\phi\colon\mathcal H\to\mathcal K$ be an isometry
    61	and set $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$.  If $N_h$ is the unitary-conjugated extension of
    62	a measurement operator $M_h$, then the exact identity is
    63	\[
    64	  \phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ=QN_h,
    65	\]
    66	not merely $N_h$.  Thus comparison of $N_h$ with an ideal projector must be
    67	combined with control of $(I-Q)\Delta$ on the ideal comparison state
    68	$\Delta$.
    69	
    70	\section{Numerical defects in the source proof}
    71	
    72	Lines~1715--1742 of
    73	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
    74	construct $H_X,H_Z$ and identify $H_XH_Z$ with the EPR projection.  The norm
    75	estimate at lines~1743--1750 gives
    76	$\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert\leq\sqrt\delta$.  At lines~1753--1757 the
    77	source substitutes $\delta$ inside the reverse triangle inequality
    78	\cite[lines~1715--1783]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  That replacement is not valid for
    79	small $\delta$.  The desired lower bound on
    80	$\langle H_W^2\rangle$ follows directly from $H_W^2\geq2H_W-I$, as above.
    81	
    82	The triangle inequality yields
    83	\[
    84	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert\leq2\sqrt\delta,
    85	\]
    86	so its square is at most $4\delta$.  Line~1761 instead bounds that square by
    87	$2\sqrt\delta$ without a stated restriction.  This inequality follows when
    88	$\delta\leq1/4$; for larger error the theorem is made trivial by enlarging the
    89	universal constant.  The same small-error split ensures that the projected
    90	vector defined at lines~1769--1773 is nonzero before it is normalized.  These
    91	are local numerical repairs and do not weaken the extraction conclusion.
    92	
    93	\section{The range-projection obligation}
    94	
    95	Lines~1827--1858 prove state-dependent closeness for the concrete operators
    96	obtained by conjugating the original measurement with the swap unitaries.
    97	Lines~1864--1875 then define isometries by adjoining EPR pairs and applying
    98	those unitaries, and immediately state the corresponding closeness for
    99	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger$.  The omitted range projection makes this implication
   100	non-definitional \cite[lines~1827--1875]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   101	
   102	Let $\Psi$ be the original state and suppose $\phi\Psi$ is close to the ideal
   103	state $\Delta$.  Since $Q\phi\Psi=\phi\Psi$ and $Q$ is a contraction, the
   104	triangle inequality bounds $(I-Q)\Delta$ by the state-extraction error.  Using
   105	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ$, split
   106	\[
   107	  (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
   108	  =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
   109	\]
   110	where $T_h$ is the ideal Pauli projector.  Summing squared norms over $h$
   111	uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
   112	The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.
   113	
   114	This transfer is an open proof obligation for the next extraction stage.  It
   115	must be a theorem derived from the concrete swap unitaries, transformed-state
   116	estimate, and operator comparisons.  It must not be stored as a bridge field,
   117	residual assumption, or hypothesis of the source-labelled soundness theorem.
   118	
   119	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
   120	
   121	The proof of Lemma~\path{lem:qld-unitary} and the soundness proof in
   122	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex} use the corrected
   123	positive-contraction estimate, make the small-error case distinction explicit,
   124	and isolate the range-projection calculation.  The chapter therefore preserves
   125	the source's state and observable conclusions while exposing the omitted
   126	argument.
   127	
   128	The structure \path{ExtractionWitness} in
   129	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/Unitary.lean} contains only the two-sided
   130	unitarity equations for the concrete swap maps, a normalized auxiliary state,
   131	the transformed-state estimate, and the two-player Pauli-projector comparison.
   132	The theorem \path{exists_extractionWitness} concludes the existence of this
   133	data at the explicit extraction scale from the projective strategy and its
   134	\path{GlobalPairWitness}; it assumes no range-projection transfer, bridge, or
   135	residual package.  Thus these declarations match the Stage~4.2 extraction
   136	lemma, including the corrected numerical estimates, but do not formalize the
   137	later passage to the isometries in the soundness theorem.  No declaration yet
   138	states that passage.
   139	
   140	Issue~\#19 owns this concrete Stage~4.2 interface and discrepancy record.
   141	\ghissue{47} owns the Stage~4.3 proof of
   142	\path{exists_extractionWitness} and the separate range-projection theorem
   143	needed by \path{pauli_soundness}; that theorem must be derived from the
   144	concrete data rather than stored in the witness.
   145	
   146	\section{Conclusion}
   147	
   148	The printed triangle calculation has repairable numerical errors, and the
   149	last passage from unitaries to isometries omits a genuine range-projection
   150	argument.  Neither defect is a counterexample to Pauli soundness.  The former
   151	is corrected by positive-contraction inequalities and a small-error split;
   152	the latter remains a named downstream proof obligation whose hypotheses are
   153	already supplied by the extraction lemma.

   402	\begin{remark}[Two steps in the source proof of the extraction lemma]\label{rem:qld-unitary-triangle-slip}

1	# Mathematical Language Guidelines
     2	
     3	MIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing
     4	the formalization with the paper and blueprint.
     5	
     6	This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
     7	naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
     8	`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.
     9	
    10	## Scope
    11	
    12	These guidelines apply to:
    13	
    14	- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
    15	- module docstrings;
    16	- declaration docstrings;
    17	- documentation-visible section comments;
    18	- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
    19	- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
    20	- issue titles and issue bodies;
    21	- PR titles and PR descriptions.
    22	
    23	## Source of Truth
    24	
    25	Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:
    26	
    27	1. `references/ldt-paper/`
    28	2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
    29	3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files
    30	
    31	When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
    32	example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
    33	projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.
    34	
    35	## Reference Notation And Terminology
    36	
    37	The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
    38	reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
    39	docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
    40	without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.
    41	
    42	When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
    43	location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
    44	first applicable location in the following order:
    45	
    46	1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
    47	   differs from the paper;
    48	2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
    49	   family of declarations in that file;
    50	3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
    51	   blueprint;
    52	4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
    53	   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.
    54	
    55	The explanation should say:
    56	
    57	- the notation or term used in the paper;
    58	- the Lean object or name which represents it;
    59	- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
    60	- the scope in which the replacement should be used.
    61	
    62	A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
    63	where future readers can learn it.
    64	
    65	Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
    66	should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
    67	rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.
    68	
    69	## Naming Norm
    70	
    71	Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
    72	conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
    73	assembled.
    74	
    75	Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
    76	`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
    77	uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
    78	such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
    79	clearer phrase.
    80	
    81	This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
    82	Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
    83	blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
    84	mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
    85	number, or implementation history.
    86	
    87	### Concrete examples
    88	
    89	The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
    90	codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
    91	others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
    92	process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
    93	assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
    94	paper or blueprint would recognize.
    95	
    96	| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
    97	|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
    98	| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
    99	| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
   100	| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
   101	| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
   102	| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
   103	| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
   104	| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
   105	| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
   106	| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
   107	| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |
   108	
   109	An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
   110	phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
   111	In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.
   112	
   113	File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
   114	named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
   115	exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.
   116	
   117	### Shared helpers
   118	
   119	When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
   120	more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
   121	shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
   122	ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
   123	call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.
   124	
   125	Procedure:
   126	
   127	1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   128	   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   129	   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   130	   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   131	   explicit argument.
   132	2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   133	   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   134	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   135	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   136	   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
   137	3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   138	   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
   139	4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   140	   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   141	   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   142	   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   143	   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   144	   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
   145	5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   146	   blueprint location it supports.
   147	
   148	### Legacy identifier treatment
   149	
   150	If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
   151	describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
   152	identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
   153	in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.
   154	
   155	Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   156	public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
   157	shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
   158	blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.
   159	
   160	## Review Checklist
   161	
   162	Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
   163	documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.
   164	
   165	- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
   166	      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
   167	      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
   168	      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
   169	      implementation-phase labels)?
   170	- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
   171	      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
   172	      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
   173	      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
   174	      source does not use them that way?
   175	- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
   176	      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
   177	      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
   178	      that order of preference?
   179	- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
   180	      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
   181	      construction they support?
   182	- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
   183	      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
   184	      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
   185	- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
   186	      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
   187	      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
   188	      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
   189	- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
   190	      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
   191	      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
   192	      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.
   193	
   194	Review-fix PRs touching a surface covered by an active audit should read the
   195	relevant audit before changing names or prose.
   196

   207	## 8. Concurrency
   208	
   209	| Lock | Key | Cancellation |
   210	|---|---|---|
   211	| review | PR id | none — a queued run waits, then re-checks the head |
   212	| fix (`autofix.md`) | branch | supersession sentinel |
   213	
   214	The split of keys is inherited (`pr-review.yml:18-20` groups by PR number with
   215	`cancel-in-progress: false`; `auto-fix.yml:259-261` groups by head branch with
   216	`cancel-in-progress: true`) and it matters: cancelling a review wastes the
   217	tokens already spent and produces nothing, whereas cancelling a superseded fix
   218	saves a write to a branch that has already moved.
   219	
   220	Locks are directories under `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/` holding the
   221	holder's pid — `flock(1)` does not exist on macOS.  A lock whose holder is gone
   222	is reclaimed.  After acquiring the review lock, `review.sh` re-reads the local
   223	tip and the remote PR head: a fix commit that landed while this run queued
   224	invalidates the review, and the run exits without a verdict rather than
   225	describing a commit that is no longer head.  The same check runs again after
   226	the agent returns; a head that moved during the review makes the result stale
   227	and forbids publication, leaving the raw output in the runtime cache.
   228	
   229	`review.sh` also refuses to start while a fix lock is held for the branch.
   230	The two tools share one worktree here, where GitHub gave each job a fresh
   231	checkout; without this cross-check the reviewer would read a tree being
   232	rewritten under it.

   334	Exit codes: `0` reviewed or intentionally skipped · `1` usage/environment ·
   335	`3` gate blocked (CI not green for this head) · `4` no parseable verdict.
   336	Code 3 publishes nothing at all — the missing green `local-review/summary` is
   337	the block.  Only code 4 publishes a `failure` `local-review/summary`, and
   338	neither publishes a review.
   339	
   340	Artefacts:
   341	
   342	| Path | Committed | Contents |
   343	|---|---|---|
   344	| the exact-head `COMMENT` review on the PR | on GitHub | combined verdict, ledger, prose |
   345	| `local-review/summary` on the head SHA | on GitHub | the gate-readable verdict |
   346	| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/` | no | diff, prompts, raw agent output |
   347	| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/review-<pr>.lock` | no | the review lock |
   348	
   349	Every codex invocation goes through `local/bin/dispatch.sh` when it exists, so
   350	the session is named, captured to `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl` and
   351	summarised into `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`
   352	(`local/protocols/sessions.md`).  Without the dispatcher, `review.sh` falls
   353	back to a direct `codex exec` and says loudly that the session will not appear
   354	in the registry — an untracked session is lost research data, so the fallback
   355	is a degradation, not an alternative.  `dispatch.sh` enforces
   356	`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` for reviewer-role sessions independently; the two checks
   357	agreeing is intentional redundancy.
   358	
   359	Missing pieces degrade with a message, never silently: missing CI statuses
   360	block, no `worktree-setup.sh` warns about a cold build cache, no codex CLI is a
   361	hard error.  A GitHub failure is fatal — a verdict that cannot be published is
   362	not a verdict.
   363	
   364	## 12. Deliberately not ported
   365	
   366	Untouched-code or new-mechanism findings are "out of scope -> issue #N".
   367	
   368	* **Provider matrix** (`CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS` → per-provider jobs).
   369	  One reviewer session; the cascade
   370	  `CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS > CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER > anthropic` becomes
   371	  `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL > MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL > the dispatcher's default`.
   372	* **Fork check** (`head_repository.full_name != repo` → skip).  Every PR here
   373	  comes from a branch of this single repository.
   374	* **Thread resolution via `mcp__github__resolve_review_thread`.**  Replaced by
   375	  the ledger checkbox; the reviewer is told not to attempt it.
   376	* **`allowed-tools` presets and `allowed-tools.json`.**  codex sandbox modes
   377	  (`read-only` for review, `workspace-write` for fixes) carry the same intent
   378	  with a coarser grain: read-only genuinely prevents writes, which the
   379	  allow-list only approximated.
   380	* **`id-token`/OAuth plumbing, `LionSR/agent-ci-actions`, plugin marketplaces.**
   381	  Local codex configuration replaces them (`.codex/`, `local/protocols/sessions.md`).
   382	
   383	
   384	## 12. Round cap and operator adjudication (2026-08-30)
   385

384	## 12. Round cap and operator adjudication (2026-08-30)
   385	
   386	A PR receives at most **four** full review rounds. From the fifth round on,
   387	the operator may close the loop by adjudication instead of iteration:
   388	
   389	1. every remaining finding is either fixed, or converted to a tracked issue;
   390	   the operator posts an **ADJUDICATION comment** on the PR — a body starting
   391	   with `ADJUDICATION`, carrying `head=<final_head>`, and listing the last
   392	   round's findings with every box ticked and a one-line disposition each
   393	   (`fixed in <commit>` / `deferred to issue #NNNN: <reason>` /
   394	   `moot: <reason>`);
   395	2. the comment is the record; nothing local is written;
   396	3. the merge commit names the adjudication and the issues created;
   397	4. `pr_merge.py --adjudicated` accepts it in place of a clean verdict, and
   398	   only for the current head — a stale `head=` is a refusal.
   399	
   400	Nothing is dropped silently: an adjudicated finding lives on as an issue.
   401	This mirrors the parent's combined bot-fix iteration cap with a single
   402	terminal review (pr-review.yml:69-72). See EVOLUTION.md for the trigger.
   403	
   404	## 13. Evidence follows the diff: carry-forward across a fresh-base (2026-09-04)
   405	
   406	The merge gate's fresh-base rule (issues-prs.md, gate 2b) moves a PR's head
   407	every time `main` advances, but a merge of `main` into the branch does not
   408	change the PR's own patch.  `review.sh` therefore compares a whitespace-
   409	sensitive hash of the patch (the diff without its `index`/hunk-header lines,
   410	so hunk positions may move but no byte of content may) with that of every
   411	earlier reviewed head of the same PR whose review is bound to that head and
   412	published by the lane's account; on a match it republishes that head's verdict
   413	and ledger as the exact-head review of the new head, marked "Carried forward
   414	from <sha>" (marker `<!-- mipstarre-review-carried from=<sha> -->`; a carried
   415	review is not a review round and is never itself a carry source), and posts the matching
   416	`local-review/summary` — without dispatching the reviewer.  Adverse verdicts
   417	are carried too, so an adjudication at the new head remains possible.  Any
   418	change to the patch (a repair, a conflict resolution) yields a different
   419	patch-id and a real review.  `--force-review` bypasses the fast path.
